hints.title: Match the term numbers
hints.body: Use a for the shared first term, d for the arithmetic difference and r for the geometric ratio. Write the specified terms in each progression.
hints.recap: The nth arithmetic term contains n−1 increments.
hints.pitfall: The two progressions use different term positions.
hints.pause: Equate the corresponding terms to get two equations.

recall.reminder: The nth arithmetic term contains n−1 increments.

hints.title: Remove the arithmetic difference
hints.body: Multiply your two equations by suitable numbers so subtracting them removes d. Use the nonzero sum to check whether a can be zero.
hints.recap: Eliminating d leaves an equation for the geometric ratio.
hints.pitfall: Check before dividing by a variable quantity.
hints.pause: Solve the resulting equation in r.

recall.reminder: Eliminating d leaves an equation for the geometric ratio.

hints.title: Use the sum to infinity
hints.body: A nonzero geometric progression has a sum to infinity only when |r|<1. Check your ratio candidates, then use S=a1−r.
hints.recap: Convergence is a condition on the common ratio.
hints.pitfall: An algebraic root can fail the convergence requirement.
hints.pause: Choose the allowed ratio and find the first term.

recall.reminder: Convergence is a condition on the common ratio.

solution:
Let the AP be a,a+d,a+2d,… and the GP be a,ar,ar2,…. The matching terms give ar=a+3d and ar2=a+5d. Since the GP sums to 12, a≠0.

Eliminate d: 5ar−3ar2=2a. Dividing by a and rearranging gives 3r2−5r+2=(3r−2)(r−1)=0. Convergence excludes r=1, leaving r=23.

Now a1−23=12, so 3a=12 and a=4, option D. For example d=−49 gives the required AP terms 4,83,169, confirming the match.
knowledgePattern: Link nonconsecutive AP terms to consecutive GP terms
